The compact base projection meets the lattice coset in finitely many points, so the placed generators form a compact finite union and their convex hull is compact. This hull stays inside Q and projects exactly to conv P, which lies in A and F.

For every lattice base in conv P, the hull fiber is nonempty. In the nonempty-retention case this and containment in Q force membership in P. In the positive-volume case fix any convex representation of the base and vary the fiber with a positive coefficient while holding all other input points fixed. The hull contains a translate of that fiber scaled by the coefficient, with positive volume. Thus membership in P follows even at boundary lattice bases. Outside conv P the hull fiber is empty. At a retained base the whole original fiber was included, so both set inclusions hold, including zero-volume retained fibers in the nonempty-retention case.

A positive-volume retained fiber yields every vertical direction. The linear directions of the hull project onto A-p0, so the hull has affine dimension t+s. The full lattice intersection in A is p0+(L intersect (A-p0)). The intersection is discrete, contains t independent lattice differences, and lies in a t-plane. It has rank t and is saturated because a real vector subspace is closed under division by a nonzero integer. The selected differences need not themselves generate the full intersection lattice.

In the chart the base lattice is counted by bijection and the continuous coordinates are unchanged. Each fiber and its intersection with a transported closed cap have unchanged s-volume, with no covolume factor.

A containing ambient closed halfspace restricts to a proper closed relative halfspace or the whole relative space. The latter has full retained mass, so it does not lower the infimum. Every proper relative halfspace extends by extending its affine functional. The same restriction works from the larger ambient space for a coarse slice, including the case of constant restriction on the slice. Original cap mass is at least retained cap mass at each fixed retained candidate, and null fibers contribute zero to every cap.

For t>0 the identified hull is full-dimensional and has exactly the sampled mass T_P, so multiplying the assumed normalized bound by T_P gives the asserted raw bound. For t=0, P has one positive fiber. The full-mass metronoid density is one almost everywhere, hence its point is the centroid and the accepted continuous bound gives Gamma_s T_P.
